newsitem.title: USA: CME's TIIE futures debut sees small volume.
newsitem.headline: CME's TIIE futures debut sees small volume.

text.p: The debut of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's latest emerging market contract, Mexican TIIE interest rate futures, saw small volume on Thursday.

The exchange launched futures and options on the 28-day Mexican Equilibrium Interbank Interest rates (TIIE) at 0800 CDT/1300 GMT Thursday, two weeks after the debut of 91-day Mexican Treasury bill (Cetes) products.
Preliminary volume estimates showed Mexican Cetes futures traded 63 contracts on Thursday, compared with 83 on Wednesday. TIIE futures traded 25 contracts.
Cetes and TIIE options did not trade.
The CME said these debt instruments round out the exchange's Mexico portfolio traded on the Growth and Emerging Markets (GEM) division.
GEM traders said interest from Mexican banks was bound to perk up as the contracts become more established.

CME economist Norman Mains, in an interview Wednesday with Reuters Financial Television, noted that peso futures got off to a slow start but have steadily gained interest since their April 1995 launch. Mexican peso futures traded an estimated 6,568 contracts on Thursday.
Other GEM Mexico instruments, however, have been less successful.
According to CME volume statistics, futures and options on Mexican par Brady bonds did not trade Wednesday, nor did futures on the Mexican IPC stock index.
Mains said the exchange was aiming for volume in Cetes and TIIE to rise to 1,000 contracts a day.
"If we could do, say, 1,000 a day after three months, we'd be pleased," Mains said.
